notBlocking.summary: An entry’s block runs on through any two-space-indented line that is not an entry, so a closing prose paragraph is glued to the last entry: in the skeleton’s own --help, “Every text mode then ends with one `next:` line …” sits under --quiet with no blank between; and a flag written with one space after it (`-o, --out <path> the output file`) folds into the flag above. 315 such lines in 76 of the 116 adopted headers. Nothing is lost (only blank lines are added, and the docs describe the block this way), but it works against the ask’s aim of letting the eye track entries.

Human mode only; nothing unsafe.
notBlocking.repro: report() in-process with mark ('a' + U+0301 x200) x8 -> summary line 1614 units long.
notBlocking.acceptance: A second cap on code points (say 32) after the grapheme cut, or a Known limit naming it.

notBlocking.summary: runtimeMarkOf builds a new Intl.Segmenter for every item that has a mark: 20 000 marked items render in 169 ms against 14 ms unmarked (about 8 microseconds an item).
notBlocking.repro: report() in-process over 20 000 items with mark 🟢 -> 169 ms; the same items without a mark -> 14 ms.
notBlocking.acceptance: One segmenter at module scope (a fence change: bundle it with the next revision), or leave as is.

knownLimits: A mark may still hold other invisible format characters (U+200B, U+2060, U+00AD); the docs name only the three bidi marks, so nothing promised is broken.
TERM is compared exactly: TERM=DUMB, an empty TERM and an unset TERM on a terminal bold, as Node’s own colour reading does for those values.
A Node built without Intl would throw (exit 3) on the first item with a mark; official builds carry full ICU.
A `Commands (…):` heading’s names are spaced but not bold (the optional half of the first receipt’s FU1, not taken).
